title: Upward ask script and risk mitigation notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Prep for 1:1 w/ manager (end of March). Goal: clear upward ask for role elevation and comp alignment + concrete timeline if not approved now.

High-level ask (one-liner):
- Request promotion to Senior People Partner (L5) + 12-18% comp alignment (market mid for our geo) OR a timebound plan with measurable milestones for conversion within 6 months.

Why now (evidence bullets):
- H1 hiring program: reduced time-to-hire from 42 -> 28 days (avg) for IC roles; hiring velocity metric in our dashboard (see linked artifact).
- Onboarding revamp: new 30/60/90 playbook adopted by 4 teams, onboarding NPS moved +14 pts for new hires (measured q4->q1).
- Ops automation: shipped offer/acceptance flow changes that cut manual HR touchpoints by ~35% and decreased offer errors to <1%.
- Cross-team impact: partnered with Eng PM to launch role calibration framework that influenced two org-level salary adjustments.
- Leadership: run biweekly manager office hours; coached 6 new managers through their first hires (direct feedback captured).

Key metrics to cite verbally:
- Time-to-hire improvement: -33% (42d -> 28d).
- Onboarding NPS delta: +14.
- Manual touches reduced: -35% (quantified from pre/post audit).
- Number of managers coached: 6 (direct client feedback).

Primary script (30–60s opener):
- "Thanks for making time. I want to share where I've focused work this last 9 months, the measurable outcomes we've shipped, and a concrete request: a promotion to Senior People Partner with comp aligned to market mid in our region. If that's not possible straight away, I'd like a clear, timebound development plan with milestones and a target review in 6 months."

Negotiation anchors (numbers):
- Ideal: promotion + 15% comp uplift (market mid).
- Acceptable: promotion now with 8% comp uplift + guaranteed 6-month comp review.
- Alternative: no promotion now, 10% one-time bonus + promotion target in 6 months tied to X/Y/Z milestones.

Milestones (if manager asks for development plan):
- Milestone A (60 days): complete cross-functional calibration playbook adoption in two remaining teams; present results at monthly People Ops sync.
- Milestone B (90 days): lead one DEI hiring pilot with metrics for slates and candidate diversity improved by 20%.
- Milestone C (180 days): demonstrate sustained hiring velocity and onboarding NPS improvements and deliver a stakeholder feedback report.

Risk mitigation (if ask denied or delayed):
- Immediate: ask for explicit reasons (skills, impact, budget) and capture them in writing.
- Escalation plan: request a follow-up with manager + HRBP + direct skip (only if manager open to it).
- Development support: ask for assigned mentor, specific stretch projects, and access to leadership training budget.
- Timeline fallback: propose a 6-month checkpoint with pre-agreed metrics and a written note in my file.

Manager objections & prepared replies: 
- Objection: "Budget constraints."
  - Reply: "I understand. Can we explore a phased approach (bonus now, comp review in 6 months) or identify non-comp levers (title, stretch remit, mentor access) that we can commit to?"
- Objection: "Need more leadership scope evidence."
  - Reply: "I can lead the DEI hiring pilot and present outcomes; let's define the brief together so it's measurable within 90 days."
- Objection: "Timing/promotion cycle."
  - Reply: "If promotion cycle timing is the blocker, can we get a formal development plan plus an early review outside the cycle based on milestones?"

Practiced lines (short):
- "Here are 3 measurable results I shipped that I think map to Senior People Partner expectations."
- "I want to be explicit about what I need from you: title change, comp alignment, or a written 6-month plan with milestones."
- "If the ask isn't possible now, I'd appreciate a firm timeline and a sponsor to help unblock."

Evidence checklist to have open in meeting:
- Hiring dashboard (link) filtered to my partner teams (TTH chart).
- Onboarding NPS raw responses + summary.
- Automation audit doc (before/after manual touches).
- Manager feedback emails/snippets (redacted).
- Two stakeholder Slack threads that highlight cross-org impact.

Follow-up steps post-meeting:
- Send recap email within 24h with agreed next steps and deadlines.
- If milestones agreed, create a shared Trello/Notion page and invite manager + HRBP.
- Set calendar reminders for 30/90/180 checkpoints.

Personal talk-track experiments (tone probes):
- Direct factual: lead with numbers (best for analytic managers).
- Story-first: short narrative about a hire we saved and how it scaled (best for relational managers).
- Hybrid: 1 sentence story then 2 metrics.

Emotional prep notes (internal):
- Breathing cue: 3 slow inhales before opening line.
- If manager hesitates, slow down and re-center on agreed shared goals (team health, retention).
- Remind self: objective evidence > emotion; keep ask framed as partnership not demand.

Open questions to ask manager (if they don't volunteer):
- "What would you need to see in 90 days to be comfortable supporting this promotion?"
- "Are there budget cycles or org signals I should be aware of?"
- "Who would you suggest as a sponsor or reviewer for my promotion case?"

Draft recap email template (to copy after meeting):
- Subject: Recap + next steps from promotion conversation
- Body: Thank you + 3 bullets (what we agreed, owner, timeline) + attach evidence links + propose next checkpoint date.

Notes / rough rehearsal bullets:
- Practice: 2x run-through w/ Samir (role-play manager pushback).
- Keep language concise; manager 1:1s often 20–25 mins.
- Ask for written confirmation of any commitments (email ok).

Back-pocket alternatives if internal route blocks:
- Consider exploring market benchmark roles externally as reference (informal).
- Seek lateral stretch into People Strategy project with clear outcomes.

Next actions (today):
- Finalize evidence bundle + dashboard filters.
- Run 2 practice calls with Samir & Noah.
- Block 30 min on manager calendar (end of March window).

-- end of scratchpad --

(Loose style on purpose; save final script once manager style confirmed.)
